title: Prospective cohort study to identify immunological signatures in chronic inflammatory diseases of the central nervous system and neurological manifestations of post-viral syndromes, with a particular focus on post-COVID syndrome
summary:
Inflammatory diseases of the brain and spinal cord, such as multiple sclerosis, and persistent nerve-related complaints after viral infections, such as after a coronavirus infection, vary greatly from person to person. The reasons are still poorly understood. A long-lasting misregulation of the immune system is thought to play an important role.

In this study, we follow patients of the Department of Neurology at St. Josef-Hospital Bochum and healthy volunteers for one year. We record examination results, questionnaires and tests. With consent, blood samples and possibly other samples are stored in coded form. The aim is to find immune patterns that match certain diseases or disease courses and thus, in the long term, to improve diagnosis and treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
1. At least one of the following:
- chronic inflammatory disease of the central nervous system (e.g. multiple sclerosis, NMOSD, MOGAD, autoimmune encephalitis), irrespective of a preceding viral infection; or
- new-onset, persistent neurological, cognitive, autonomic or systemic symptoms temporally associated with a (suspected) preceding viral infection (e.g. SARS-CoV-2, influenza, EBV, VZV, enteroviruses), including post-COVID syndrome and ME/CFS; or
- exacerbation of a pre-existing chronic inflammatory CNS disease temporally associated with a (suspected) viral infection.
Laboratory confirmation of the infection is not mandatory if a plausible temporal and clinical association is documented.
2. Capacity to consent and written informed consent.
3. Willingness to participate in follow-up assessments.

Healthy controls:
- no known disease of the central or peripheral nervous system
- no acute or recent (≤ 4 weeks) infection
- written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- lack of consent or lack of capacity to consent without an authorised legal representative
- participation in an interventional clinical trial that could substantially affect the clinical, functional or immunological parameters collected in the registry
- severe psychiatric disorder precluding valid data collection
- contraindication to all planned assessments
- other, non-neurological autoimmune disease
- history of malignancy
- acute infection at the time of enrolment
- treatment with intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIg) within the last 6 months
